definitions.explanation: Short form of {総理大臣|そうりだいじん}, the prime minister of Japan. This abbreviated form is very commonly used in everyday speech and media.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{総理|そうり}が{決|き}まった。
examples.english: A new prime minister has been decided.

examples.japanese: {総理|そうり}が{記者会見|きしゃかいけん}を{開|ひら}いた。
examples.english: The prime minister held a press conference.

examples.japanese: {総理|そうり}の{支持率|しじりつ}が{大幅|おおはば}に{下|さ}がっている。
examples.english: The prime minister's approval rating has dropped significantly.

notes:
USAGE:
Abbreviation of {総理大臣|そうりだいじん} (prime minister). In news and conversation, {総理|そうり} is far more common than the full form. When addressing or referring to a specific prime minister, the pattern is surname + {総理|そうり} (e.g., {田中|たなか}{総理|そうり}). The formal title used in official documents is {内閣総理大臣|ないかくそうりだいじん}.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {首相|しゅしょう}: prime minister (used more in news reporting, applies to any country's PM)
- {大統領|だいとうりょう}: president (of a country)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {総理大臣|そうりだいじん}: prime minister (full form)
- {総理|そうり}{官邸|かんてい}: prime minister's official residence
- {総理|そうり}の{支持率|しじりつ}: prime minister's approval rating
- {総理|そうり}に{就任|しゅうにん}する: take office as prime minister
